scenarios.title: The loudest customer becomes the market
scenarios.prompt: One large customer describes a painful workflow problem. The roadmap discussion treats that story as proof that most users need the same feature.
scenarios.question: What evidence should be checked before reprioritizing the roadmap?

options.text: How common the workflow and pain are across the relevant customer population.
How strongly the customer repeats the request in the next meeting.
Whether the story is memorable enough to explain to executives.

scenarios.explanation: A vivid case can be important without being representative. A base-rate check asks how often the problem occurs and for whom.
missingEvidence: Number of affected customers and users.
Severity and frequency of the problem.
Evidence from customers who do not request the feature.
scenarios.evidenceNote: Availability bias may increase the story’s weight, but a single strategic customer can still justify action for commercial reasons. Those reasons should be explicit.
scenarios.nextAction: Estimate prevalence and value before comparing the feature with other roadmap options.

scenarios.title: Too much code to stop now
scenarios.prompt: A feature has consumed eight months of work. New research shows limited demand, but the team argues that stopping would waste the investment.
scenarios.question: Which question should drive the next decision?

options.text: How much effort has already been spent compared with the original budget?
Would we fund the remaining work today, based on future cost, value and uncertainty?
How embarrassing would cancellation look to the steering committee?

scenarios.explanation: Past work cannot be recovered. The incremental-value check evaluates only the future consequences of continuing, stopping or changing direction.
missingEvidence: Switching and cancellation consequences that still lie in the future.
scenarios.evidenceNote: Escalation of commitment is a plausible lens because past investment is used as a reason for further investment. Relevant future switching costs should not be ignored.
scenarios.nextAction: Write a future-only business case for the next release step.
